definition: The Internet of Musical Things (also known as IoMusT) is a research area that aims to bring Internet of Things connectivity to musical and artistic practices.
details: Moreover, it encompasses concepts coming from music computing, ubiquitous music, human-computer interaction, artificial intelligence, augmented reality, virtual reality, gaming, participative art, and new interfaces for musical expression. From a computational perspective, IoMusT refers to local or remote networks embedded with devices capable of generating and/or playing musical content.

explainer.lead: IoMusT is a research area bringing Internet of Things connectivity to musical and artistic practices. It matters because it links music computing, interaction, AI, and extended reality into networked musical systems.

tiers.eli5: Imagine instruments and music gear that talk to each other over a network, like smart home devices but for making music.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers build local or remote networks of devices that generate or play musical content, drawing on ubiquitous music, HCI, and new musical interfaces. A pitfall is that musical latency and timing requirements are far stricter than in typical IoT deployments.
tiers.paperLevel: Computationally, IoMusT refers to local or remote networks embedded with devices capable of generating and/or playing musical content; it also draws on music computing, ubiquitous music, HCI, AI, AR, VR, gaming, participative art, and new interfaces for musical expression. Music timing constraints are a known practical limit.

explainer.example: A networked ensemble where several connected devices each generate or play musical content over a local network.
